Restoration Shaman Rotation in 

Restoration Shaman is a very straightforward spec. Your focus will be on getting as much value as you can out of the short cooldowns and properly picking targets for your Riptide s and filler casts. The basics are simple but there is room for optimization once you start getting comfortable with the kit. These are the most important things to keep in mind:

 

 

 
 
 Pick Your Targets Correctly: Effects like Undercurrent , Deluge , Flow of the Tides , and Tidewaters greatly benefit from having as many Riptide s active as possible so you should always aim to put Riptide on people that don't already have it. Mastery: Deep Healing and our casted heals being directly targeted also means that correctly picking people that need the most healing and are at the lowest health percentage will increase the value of everything you do.
 

 

 
 

 
 Use Your Short Cooldowns On Cooldown: Restoration Shaman has a wide list of short cooldown spells that do a variety of different things, but they all have in common that the best way to use them is to press them early and often if any healing is needed. Unleash Life , Healing Rain , Surging Totem , Downpour , Nature's Swiftness , Ancestral Swiftness , and Healing Stream Totem and its Stormstream Totem procs all are more valuable if you use them as many times as possible during combat and focus on not missing out on casts of them.
 

 

 
 

 
 Manage Your Mana: The amount of mana you use can vary a lot depending on what spells you choose to cast outside of cooldowns: Healing Wave is very cheap but only heals a single target and is a bit more likely to overheal while Chain Heal is much more expensive but spreads the healing across multiple target picked in the best possible way. How much do you value each of these things can vary depending on the content you're doing and for how long you need to keep healing without running out of mana. Talents like Resurgence and Calm Waters can aleviate issues but at the cost of losing other alternatives. Pick the correct tool for the job at any given moment and understand the flow of your mana so you can keep healing for as long as it is needed. 
 

 

Restoration Shaman Starter Guide

 Best Restoration Shaman Rotation

The priority focuses on three things: Using the short cooldowns as much as possible, properly utilizing all the short buffs you generate, and balancing Healing Wave and Chain Heal to maximize healing while optimizing mana.

Below, we break down the main priority lists for Restoration Shaman: Raid Healing and Mythic+ Healing.

 Hero Talent Master Switches 

 You can use the master switches below to flip the entire page's options to your selected choice.

 checked]Totemic]Farseer

 
 Best Restoration Shaman Raid Healing Rotation

 On raids mana can be a concern so proper pacing of your Chain Heal casts is important to make sure you can keep healing for the whole encounter. Your short cooldowns are very efficient and should be prioritized above filler casts as long as doing so wouldn't make you waste some of the buffs they apply.

Normal Priority

 
Use all your Stormstream Totem procs 

Keep Riptide on cooldown 

Use Ancestral Swiftness 

Cast Unleash Life 

Maintain Healing Rain 

Keep Healing Stream Totem on cooldown 

Cast Chain Heal or Healing Wave 
 

 
Stormstream Totem Usage

One of your biggest sources of healing is Stormstream Totem and the vast majority of the procs will come from using Ancestral Swiftness . You can also get a proc every time you cast Riptide but these will be somewhat rare and you can't depend on them.

It is important to know that the buff that lets you cast Stormstream Totem lasts 60 seconds, so you don't need to use them immediately after you get it. It can be a good decision to save your Stormstreams for a bit to better line them up with incoming damage. As the cooldown of Ancestral Swiftness is only 30 seconds you can infinitely refresh the Stormstream Totem buff to never let it expire, but the maximum amount of stacks you can have is two. If you don't need extra healing right now but will do so in 30 seconds or one minute you should keep using Ancestral Swiftness and saving the Stormstream Totem s to use them all at the same time when they would get the most value. Do note that you will miss out on casts of Healing Stream Totem doing this but because the spell is fairly low value for this is acceptable.Because the cooldown of Nature's Swiftness matches this duration, the buff will expire just before swiftness comes back off cooldown, unless you get another proc from Riptide during it. Even in this case, because the maximum amount of Stormstream Totem stacks you can have is two, using Nature's Swiftness again before spending any of them will just result in wasting one. Furthermore trying to delay casting Stormstream Totem means you miss out on Healing Stream Totem casts which as you really don't want to do. So while you don't need to spend your procs immediately, you are heavily incentivized to do so as soon as possible.

Chain Heal vs Healing Wave

Your selection of Chain Heal or Healing Wave to fill all time not using cooldowns comes down to how many targets need healing and how much mana do you have available. Chain Heal is considerably stronger but costs significantly more mana, while Healing Wave is still very good and also very cheap. You should use Chain Heal as much as possible as mana allows if aoe healing is needed, and Healing Wave if you need to do single-target healing or need to conserve mana. This same decision applies during Ascendance , the spells are considerably stronger during it but their use cases remain the same: Chain Heal does much more healing spread across several targets, while Healing Wave costs zero mana and is better at single or two target healing.

Ascendance Sequence

During Ascendance your Chain Heal and Healing Wave become way stronger and you want to cast them as much as possible. To maximize the healing you do for the duration of the buff you want to do some preparation steps before entering into Ascendance. You want to make sure to have two stacks of Tidal Waves by using all your available Riptide s and to cast Unleash Life and Surging Totem right before pressing the cooldown. Once inside of it you want to cast your chosen spell twice, to consume the Unleash Life buffs, before using Ancestral Swiftness . Using Swiftness before this point would make you waste the cast time reduction from Unleash Life as the spell would be instant but still consume it.

After that, simply spend all the time during Ascendance casting your healing spells as many times as you can. For , because Healing Stream Totem and Stormstream Totem also cast a full-power Chain Heal that benefits from Ascendance, you should use all of your available charges of them during the cooldown. Totems have a lower global cooldown, which means you can fit many more casts into your Ascendance window this way.

If you need to heal a specific single target then you would cast Healing Wave. Any situation with at least three targets injured favors Chain Heal.

Use Nature's Swiftness 

Maintain Surging Totem

Healing Rain is harder to get value out of because there are less players but it is still worth it for effects like Deluge as long as you can have a majority of the group inside of it.

Pre-Combat Check

 Before any combat happens, it is important for Restoration Shamans to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

 Restoration Shaman Major Cooldowns

Restoration has three major healing cooldowns in its talent tree, two of which share a choice node so at any given moment you will have access to two of them. Our cooldowns range from very simple to somewhat complex and possibly convoluted; here we will cover them in depth and explain what they do and how to use them. You also have access to a couple of minor cooldowns that are still very important for optimal gameplay.

 
 Ascendance 

 Newly reworked going into Midnight, Ascendance works by enhancing your abilities for a short duration. These are the specific effects:
 
On cast, all injured allies within 20 yards will get healed. The amount of healing is fixed and gets split evenly between the targets.

Your casts of Healing Wave will always be critical strikes and also heal a second ally for 50% the amount.

Your Chain Heal s will bounce up to three additional times and the reduction per jump is down to 10% from the normal 30%.

Both Healing Wave and Chain Heal cost 25% less mana.
 

 The lower reduction on Chain Heal jumps is a very strong effect and combined with the reduced mana cost it makes Chain Heal an incredibly strong ability. Healing Wave is still preferable if you only need to heal one or two targets and it is effectively mana free. Do note that the same player can't be healed twice by different bounces of the same Chain Heal so during M+ the extra jumps won't help you at all but the jump reduction still makes the spell much better than normally.

 Each hit of Healing Wave and Chain Heal can proc Resurgence which means Ascendance in combination with it is very good for mana recovery. The guaranteed critical strikes on Healing Wave mean you will proc Resurgence on every cast and the second smaller hit also counts as it own cast so you will get two procs of the mana recovery effect every time you use the spell. This means you can effectively recover more mana than what you spend while casting Healing Wave over and over during Ascendance.

 The healing that Chain Heal can do during Ascendance is almost unmatched in raids, making Ascendance one of the strongest healer cooldowns in the game right now.

 
 Spirit Link Totem 

 Spirit Link Totem is a damage reduction cooldown, meaning the best way to get value out of it is to use it right before the group takes a big hit of damage. Aiming it at the floor will cover a medium-sized area where every friendly player inside takes 10% reduced damage and redistributes their health every second to keep everyone at the same percentage.

 It is a very good tool to keep your group alive through very high damage windows, as everyone will take reduced damage and players with weaker defensives that end up at lower health will get healed back up by the redistribution. You can also use it as a single-target emergency cooldown if someone is about to die and you don't have any other tool to react in time, Spirit Link will instantly get them back to very high health by taking away some from the healthier players around them.

 It is important to remember that the redistribution effect doesn't generate any healing. Every time it gets someone's health up, someone else's health has to go down.

 Using the redistribution effect to get a player's health back up quickly to a safe level after taking damage is still very good and can save lives, but using the spell this way means you get no value out of the damage reduction. Some level of proactivity is recommended to get maximum value.

 If you talent into Spouting Spirits , the damage reduction goes up to 15% and everyone inside the area of the totem will get healed one second after you drop it.

 
 Healing Tide Totem 

 This is the simplest cooldown in the Restoration kit. Healing Tide Totem will pulse several times over 10 seconds and heal all your allies within 40 yards. The healing is reduced beyond 5 targets, so the ability will heal each target more during dungeons than in raids. You can either reduce its cooldown with First Ascendant or increase its duration, granting extra haste with Preeminence .

 While playing Totemic , Healing Tide gains extra effects: a big increase from Splitstream , a free Chain Heal when you use it from Lively Totems , and the ability to apply Earthliving Weapon every time it heals from Primal Catalyst . All make it a much more attractive choice for Totemic than Farseer .

 You should use it every time you need to do high healing on your whole group. In raids, pre-plan usage for the most dangerous parts of the fight.

 
 Totemic Nature's Swiftness 

 Nature's Swiftness is an ability with a one-minute cooldown found in the capstone area of the Shaman class talents. It makes your next casted ability cost no mana and removes its cast time. Because the main drawback of Chain Heal is its high mana cost you can use Swiftness as a way to get extra free Chain Heals over the course of a fight. You can also use it to speed up an emergency Healing Wave in case someone is in danger of dying before you have time to finish a cast.

 The most important part of Swiftness however is the guaranteed Stormstream Totem you get when using it. Most of your Stormstreams during combat will come from using Swiftness on cooldown so it is very important that you don't hold the ability for too long or you will start losing out on valuable healing. The cooldown doesn't start until you consume the buff so don't forget to actually cast a spell as soon as possible after pressing it, you can hold the Stormstream proc for a bit longer if you don't need the healing right away.

 You can also use Nature's Swiftness to cast a damage spell instantly, but we don't recommend that.

 
 Farseer Ancestral Swiftness 

 While playing this ability transforms into Ancestral Swiftness . The main differences are a shorter cooldown, increasing the power on the ability you consume it with, and spawning an ancestor with every use. You still need to talent into the baseline Nature's Swiftness from the class tree even if you have access to Ancestral Swiftness, otherwise it will not spawn an ancestor. 

 With a reduced cooldown also comes extra Stormstream Totems, as every usage of Ancestral Swiftness will generate one the same way baseline Nature's Swiftness does. Combined with the ancestor that spawns from it this highlights the importance of using the spell on cooldown as much as possible even more.

 You should still generally consume Ancestral Swiftness with Chain Heal, but Healing Rain or even damage spells in M+ can also be options.

 
 Spiritwalker's Grace 

 Spiritwalker's Grace lets you cast abilities while moving for a short duration. This spell is very important to deal with forced movement scenarios where significant healing is still required.

 One quirk of the spell you can abuse is that whatever you are casting when the effect ends won't be immediately interrupted and can still be cast while moving. If you start one cast on the last second of the buff, you are free to finish that cast while moving even if the effect isn't present anymore. You can also activate it midway through a cast and start moving without interrupting yourself.

 Restoration Shaman Advanced Tips

Some mechanics of Restoration are not super clear simply by reading their tooltips or observing their in-game behavior. If you want to get the most out of your gameplay you must understand how your abilities actually work. Here you will find detailed explanations on the intricacies of the most relevant abilities and talents.

 
 Stormstream Totem 

 Our apex talent Stormstream Totem comes in the form of a proc that improves our next cast of Healing Stream Totem giving it a high initial wave of healing, extra targets, and an overall healing increase while it is active. Stormstream Totem does not consume a charge of Healing Stream as every time it procs it will instantly restore one charge and also increase your maximum charges by one, so you should never lose out on casts of Healing Stream because of Stormstream.

 There are two ways to proc Stormstream: The first one and most reliable is by using Nature's Swiftness or Ancestral Swiftness . Every cast of these spells will instantly generate one Stormstream so you should aim to use them as many times as possible during combat. The second way is a 6% chance every time you cast Riptide . Do note that these Riptides have to be actually casted by you so free applications from Primal Tide Core don't increase your chances.

 Once Stormstream procs you will get a 60 seconds buff that stacks up to two times, you can hold onto the buff for a decently long time in order to use it at the most appropriate moment but the longer you sit on it the more likely you are to lose out on Healing Stream casts due to not pressing the button at all. The two charges also make it very unlikely for you to miss out on procs by getting unlucky and generating one while already having one, you simply get the ability to use the ability back to back to drop two Stormstreams at the same time.

 For Stormstream will also heal one extra target at 30% power due to Splitstream and cast a free Chain Heal from Lively Totems . The spell also benefits from spec tree Healing Stream talents like Quickstream and Living Stream .

 This ability to stack up to two, the long duration of the buff, and the guaranteed proc from Swiftness gives you a lot of flexibility into how do you wanna use the totems and lets you align it properly with damage event for maximum value.

 The Stormstream Totem talent itself also increases all healing both Stormstream and Healing Stream do by 40%.

 
 Call of the Ancestors 

 The main feature of Farseer , Call of the Ancestors lets you summon ancestors by using Unleash Life and Ancestral Swiftness . These ancestors mimic your casts by using their own spells on the same target as you, increasing your healing.

 The ancestors have their own versions of the spells, so the power of their casts isn't affected by your talents. Ancestral Awakening mentions summoning an "Ancestral Spirit" on its description but this is just flavor text, the talent has no interaction with Farseer at all.

 Filler Spells 

 Restoration has two non-cooldown healing spells, Healing Wave and Chain Heal . Once all your short cooldowns are down these two spells are your only sources of healing. As of Midnight most talents that temporarily buff your next spell cast of these are gone or affect both spells equally. This means that when it comes time to cast a filler the two spells are competing with each other for your attention.

 There are some mechanics about Chain Heal worth mentioning: As soon as the cast finishes, the increases from versatility, Unleash Life , and Flow of the Tides are calculated right as the spell begins to jump. After each heal it will bounce to a new target reducing the amount of the heal by 30%. Each bounce gets increased by mastery, critical strike, Earth Shield , and Deluge independently of previous or subsequent jumps. Chain Heal is a fully smart heal and it will always pick the targets that will make it do the most effective healing. Ascendance adds three extra jumps and changes the reduction between each jump from 30% to 10% but the same target can not be healed by multiple jumps so during M+ some of them will be wasted.

 For Healing Wave the spell itself is a very simple single target heal on a very low mana cost. During Ascendance it will always critically strike and also heal a nearby ally for 50% of the amount. The extra hit from Ascendance counts as a full cast of the spell which means it can benefit from talents like Resurgence and Ancestral Awakening making it a very powerful effect.

 When it comes to numbers Chain Heal is considerably stronger than Healing Wave so it will be your default pick unless there are not enough injured targets to take full advantage of it or if your mana is running low, in those cases you should use Healing Wave . During Ascendance both spells become much stronger but the difference remains the same: Chain Heal does much more healing overall while Healing Wave is better for spot healing and recovers more mana than what it costs to cast.

 For Lively Totems will cast Chain Heal completely free and with no cast time every time you use Healing Stream Totem , Healing Tide Totem , or Spirit Link Totem which is a very strong effect as it removes the main draw backs of the spell: its mana cost and cast time.

 
 Deeply Rooted Elements 

 Deeply Rooted Elements gives you a 7% chance every time you apply a Riptide to activate Ascendance . The talent does have bad luck protection; over time the number of procs you get should normalize, though it is still possible to get streaks one way or the other. Notably it is important to make the distinction that the talent can proc on every Riptide application not cast , so abilities that apply free Riptide s like Primal Tide Core can cause procs.

 Activations of Ascendance from Deeply Rooted Elements do benefit from Preeminence and also cause the initial healing.
